source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Renal impairment routinely increases drug clearance, so doses should generally be increased to prevent subtherapeutic exposure.","B":"Kidney function is irrelevant when a drug is renally eliminated because dosing frequency alone determines systemic exposure.","C":"Reduced renal clearance can increase drug exposure, so dose or interval may need adjustment using drug-specific renal-function guidance.","D":"All renally eliminated drugs require the same fixed percentage dose reduction, regardless of the degree of impairment or drug characteristics."}}
source_row.rationale: For drugs substantially cleared by the kidneys, renal impairment can increase exposure; dosage or interval adjustments must follow drug-specific pharmacokinetic evidence and the patient's renal function.
source_row.source_detail: Final guidance addresses how impaired renal function can alter pharmacokinetics and how renal-function information should support dosage recommendations for affected drugs. FDA final guidance, March 2024; current FDA page rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: FDA — Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Renal Function
source_row.stem: A client has reduced kidney function and is prescribed a medication substantially eliminated by the kidneys. Which principle is most important?
